Make It Last A Lifetime

Caring for your wood

A good board can outlive the person who bought it — but only if it's looked after. None of this is hard. Five minutes a month is the whole job. Here's exactly what to do.

First, The Two Rules

If you remember nothing else

Never the dishwasher Heat and a long soak are the two things that destroy a wooden board. The dishwasher delivers both. It will warp, crack, and split the glue joints. Hand-wash, always.
Never let it soak Wood drinks water. Don't leave the board sitting in the sink or under a running tap. Wash it, rinse it, dry it, and stand it on edge to finish air-drying.
Everyday & Monthly

The routine

01

Wash after every use

Hot water, a drop of mild dish soap, and a sponge or soft brush. Scrub with the grain. Rinse promptly — don't let it sit. For raw meat or garlic, a little extra soap is fine; the wood's natural fibers are surprisingly antibacterial, but soap never hurts.

02

Dry it standing up

Towel it dry, then stand it on its edge or lean it against the backsplash so air reaches both faces. Drying flat on the counter traps moisture underneath and is the most common cause of a warped board. Give it an hour before you put it away.

03

Oil it about once a month

When the wood starts looking dry, dull, or thirsty — or roughly once a month with regular use — give it a coat of food-grade mineral oil. Pour a tablespoon on, spread it with a cloth or your hand, get the edges and ends, and let it soak in for a few hours or overnight. Wipe off whatever didn't absorb. End-grain boards drink more; oil those a little more often.

What oil to use Plain food-grade mineral oil (sold at any pharmacy or hardware store) or our beeswax board butter. Avoid olive, vegetable, or other cooking oils — they go rancid and will make the board smell sour over time.
04

Wax it a few times a year

Every few months, follow the oil with a board butter — a blend of mineral oil and beeswax. The wax leaves a thin protective layer that beads water and keeps the oil from washing out as fast. Buff it to a soft sheen with a clean cloth. Your board will look brand new every time.

05

Refresh stains & odors naturally

For onion or garlic smells, scrub with coarse salt and half a lemon, then rinse and dry. For light stains or a fuzzy surface after washing, sand lightly with fine (320-grit) paper along the grain and re-oil. A board is meant to be used — knife marks and a little patina are character, not damage.

At A Glance

Do & don't

Do

  • Hand-wash in warm, soapy water
  • Dry standing on edge for airflow
  • Oil monthly with food-grade mineral oil
  • Use salt & lemon for odors
  • Use both sides to wear it evenly

Don't

  • Put it in the dishwasher — ever
  • Let it soak or sit in standing water
  • Dry it flat on the counter
  • Use olive or vegetable oil (goes rancid)
  • Leave it near a heat vent or in direct sun
